# Edmund Carrow

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c7 P42](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0042), [v5 c17 P32](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0032)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Edmund  <sub>[v5 c17 P8](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

Edmund is considered the most handsome among the Hollowmere children. He has well-shaped features, straight black hair, and pale skin. His large, striking gray eyes express deep emotions and a radiant, captivating light.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c8 P25](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0025), [v5 c16 P4](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0004), [v5 c17 P6](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0006), [v5 c17 P26](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0026), [v5 c29 P8](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0008)_

## Personality

Edmund possesses a profound love of beauty, poetry, and nature, backed by a vivid imagination. He enjoys telling imaginative tales, reciting verse, and evoking strong emotional reactions in his companions. Shy and delicate, he avoids physical fights and sports, leading some peers to view him as quiet or effeminate. However, when his loved ones are insulted, he displays an unexpected, fierce courage and a strong sense of honor.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 c8 P12](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0012), [v5 c8 P27](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0027), [v5 c16 P24](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0024), [v5 c17 P16](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0016), [v5 c17 P42](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0042), [v5 c17 P57](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0057)_

- to become a poet  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>

## History

Edmund grew up at Hollowmere near Glen St. Agnes as one of the Carrow children. He frequently played with his siblings and local friends in Fern Hollow, a valley he named after a rainbow seemed to land in it. While at school, he was generally viewed as quiet and disinclined toward physical confrontation, preferring to read poetry and share stories with his friends. When Grace Ashdown challenged him to ride a pig through Glen St. Agnes, Edmund accepted to avoid backing down, subsequently taking sole blame for the stunt to protect Grace from criticism. Upon hearing Dan Coyle insult his mother's writing and call Grace derogatory names, Edmund stood up to the bully and agreed to a duel after school. Despite dreading the fight and suffering intense anxiety beforehand, Edmund engaged Dan with wild determination, winning the battle and forcing Dan to retract all his insults. Following the fight, the Rev. John Ashdown commended Edmund for defending the honor of his mother and Grace, giving Edmund the courage to finally face his fear of dental pain and get his troubling tooth extracted.
